Subject: RFI follow-up: replicate performance numbers and load scenarios

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the perf summary you provided in the RFP. Our SRE and procurement teams need more deterministic detail so we can scope our POC. Specifically can you provide: 1) the exact request mix and sequence-length distribution used for the reported throughput/latency numbers (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99), 2) the warm-up and steady-state window length, 3) hardware and model variants used (including quantization / kernel selection), 4) the concurrency pattern (open vs closed loop) and how batching was driven, and 5) steps to reproduce the runs (command-line, container tags, and any synthetic load harness).

We need answers in time for our procurement review next Wednesday. If you have a short reproducibility runbook and an XLS load matrix we can ingest, that would be ideal. Also flag any caveats (cache priming, KV cache hit assumptions, prefix caching) that change the numbers.

Can you loop in a technical contact and share an example run we could reproduce in our staging environment?

Best,
Dana

Dana—

Appreciate the clear ask. Attaching a concise reproducibility pack and a populated load matrix. High-level answers up front, with a short runbook in the attachments and a drive link for artifacts. We can also schedule a 30–45 min run-through next week and provide a live run so your SREs can reproduce.

Summary (top-line):
- Model/Test combo: rw-7b-int8 (quantized), hw: 8xA100-80GB per worker; kernel set: fused-attn-v2 + optimized-gemm.
- Concurrency: closed-loop client at 500 concurrent sessions for steady-state reporting; open-loop burst tests used maintained QPS targets.
- Sequence-length distribution: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% mid (65–256), 10% long (257–1024).
- Reported numbers: steady-state tokens/sec per cluster: 1.8M t/s; p50 latency: 32ms; p95: 120ms; p99: 420ms (at 500 concurrent sessions, throughput-target backpressure engaged). See PDF for full tables.
- Warm-up: 15 minutes (KV prefix priming + 5 cold-start iterations), steady-state sample window: 20 minutes after warm-up.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache assumed and instrumented; our numbers include a 72% KV cache-hit profile. Without prefix caching p95/p99 degrade ~1.6x.

Attachments include: populated load matrix (veridian_rfp_load_matrix.xlsx), runbook-repro-commands.sh (scripts + container tags), and redwood_perf_report_v1.pdf with raw measurements and visualization.

Caveats:
- We tuned batching to maintain latency SLO; larger batch targets increase throughput but raise p95/p99.
- Results vary across model variants and quantization modes; we can reproduce runs for fw-7b-fp16 and rw-13b-int8 if desired.

Next steps: share a time slot for a reproducibility call (we'll bring an engineer to run live).

Thanks,
Monica

Dana—

Answers inline below and we've attached an expanded runbook that contains exact commands and the container tags. We'll also pre-stage a public GCS bucket of priming payloads so you can run without sample-drift.

1) Session affinity: our closed-loop harness used an anti-affinity proxy by default (balanced allocation across replicas). For the reported runs we saw near-uniform per-replica concurrency (+/- 8% variance) with 16 replicas behind the pool (approx 31 user sessions per replica at 500 total). We have a cookie-based affinity mode implemented for sticky routing; that was not used for the quoted steady-state numbers.

2) KV cache hit derivation: the 72% figure came from sampling a 72-hour production-like trace during priming, and measuring live KV lookups during the steady-state window. The runbook includes the tracing query used (trace-id filter and sampling rate). We also include a synthetic priming set (folder: /priming/seed-72pct/) in the Drive link.

3) Priming sensitivity: p99 is sensitive to priming when the model relies on large KV prefixes. In our experiments increasing priming corpus from 10k -> 100k unique prefixes reduced p99 by ~18% in the long-tail. The runbook contains a priming-size toggles section and a simple script to generate priming payloads.

4) Container tags and ENV: image: redwood/inference:20260801-optim (sha256:7a3f...), ENV: RW_BATCH_TARGET_MS=16, RW_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=2048, RW_PREFIX_CACHE=true. These are in runbook-repro-commands.sh.

Practical notes: if you run in an on-prem environment with smaller GPU memory, use the rw-7b-int8 fragment build and set RW_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024 to avoid OOM; expect p95 to increase ~1.2x.

I'll schedule a 30-min window Wednesday 08/12 09:00 PT for a live reproduction unless you prefer a different time. Ben will join from perf; Marissa will own artifacts and deliverables.

Thanks and let us know availability.

Monica
